label: prose:intro-confinement-level
html: Confinement in the Iwahori–Hecke algebra is a discrete filtration rather than a binary predicate: each composite braid word carries a non-negative integer confinement level \ell \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} measuring the minimal number of quadratic Hecke reduction steps required to reach a trivial closure. This section proves that \ell is an invariant of the Markov equivalence class, identifies the infinite-level kernel with the cemetery group of quotient-trivial braids, and connects the confinement filtration to the Kashiwara crystal graph and Khovanov–Lauda–Rouquier (KLR) \mathbb{Z}-grading.
